title: Breakable Machine: A K–12 Classroom Game for Transformative AI Literacy Through Spoofing and eXplainable AI (XAI)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how to teach critical and transformative AI literacy in K–12 by helping students understand not only how AI systems work, but also how they fail. The authors argue that AI education should move beyond building models and instead include opportunities to interrogate brittleness, bias, reliability, and sociotechnical implications through hands-on experiences with failure.

To do this, the paper presents Breakable Machine, an XAI-based classroom game in which learners try to spoof an image classifier by changing their appearance or surroundings so that the model confidently misclassifies them. Students can also inspect saliency heatmaps and explore the training data to infer why the system behaves as it does. The game is designed for grades 4–9, roughly ages 10–15, and runs in a browser on students’ devices with a teacher-facing projector view and leaderboard.

The paper is non-empirical and focuses on the design and pedagogical rationale of the resource rather than outcome evaluation. Its main conclusion is that intentionally breaking AI systems can be a productive educational strategy for fostering AI literacy, data agency, ethical awareness, and a critical stance toward AI as a fallible sociotechnical system. The authors position misclassification and adversarial play as central learning opportunities, with empirical assessment of learning outcomes left for future work.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a design/resource paper describing a classroom game and its pedagogical rationale, not an empirical evaluation of outcomes. The paper explicitly states that empirical evaluation of learning outcomes is future work.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper proposes a potentially meaningful K-12 AI literacy intervention focused on reliability, misinformation, and overreliance, but it reports no measured effects. Impact is therefore conceptually promising but empirically unconfirmed.

interventions.use_case: XAI-based classroom spoofing game for K-12 students to trick an image classifier by manipulating appearance or environment, using a shared leaderboard and saliency heatmaps to support critical AI literacy and inquiry.

Browser-based classroom learning tool that guides students through structured image-classification experimentation, model probing, and reflection using the app interface, training-data view, and teacher controls.
